purpose: Durable current-technology candidates with explicit adopt/experiment/observe/reject decisions so Project Constellation stays current without blind upgrades.

records.fact: The current npm package is 3.53.0-build1. SQLite WASM supports OPFS persistence and current SQLite docs expose opfs, opfs-sahpool, and opfs-wl choices with different concurrency/header tradeoffs. Worker1/Promiser1 APIs are deprecated as of 2026-04-15.
records.fit: Project Constellation already has a PWA/website line and needs stronger local durability without weakening the permanent single-file Quick View.
records.benefit: A PWA-only SQLite/OPFS mirror could provide indexed durable project/research history and explicit migration/version evidence while the zero-setup HTML continues to work unchanged.
records.risks: COOP/COEP and worker requirements vary by VFS; multi-tab locking semantics differ; embedding it into the permanent single HTML would add unacceptable weight/complexity.
records.migrationPath: Keep localStorage plus snapshot import/export as the baseline. Build a PWA-only adapter behind capability detection and one-way import/export before considering bidirectional sync.
records.experiment: Prototype an isolated PWA branch that imports the 63-record catalog into SQLite WASM using a selected OPFS VFS and exports byte-identical project JSON back out.
records.acceptance: All 63 project records and user state round-trip; two-tab behavior is explicitly tested; unavailable OPFS falls back cleanly; Quick View remains dependency-free and unchanged; no canonical data is deleted or rewritten silently.

records.fact: The project ports Shimeji-ee from JRE 6 to JDK 25, uses Maven/Launch4j, adds proper DPI scaling and Windows/macOS/Linux support, and explicitly attempts backward compatibility. Recent July 2026 commits include settings reload work and dependency maintenance.
records.fit: PCX-037 requires modernization without breaking XML actions/behaviors, pack layout, window interactions, or DPI behavior.
records.benefit: Provides a maintained modern-Java reference for compatibility tests and packaging without forcing a rewrite.
records.integrationCost: low for reference tests; high for direct migration
records.risks: It is not the user-owned canonical source; direct replacement could discard custom behavior.
records.migrationPath: Resolve canonical user source first, then run identical packs/XML/window/DPI fixtures against both runtimes and port only evidence-backed improvements.
records.experiment: Create a compatibility corpus from existing packs and compare action/behavior selection, required actions, image-set discovery, drag/throw, window interaction, DPI, startup, and memory.
records.acceptance: Canonical runtime retains all existing packs and behavior; any borrowed change improves a measured problem; no pack semantic regression; Windows behavior remains correct and cross-platform additions stay optional.

records.fact: The repository is archived. Its own current status says the Qt implementation is discontinued.
records.fit: It remains useful historical research for libshijima and platform behavior but is a poor new base for a continuity-critical modernization.
records.risks: Archived/discontinued base would create maintenance debt and can lag newer compatibility fixes.
records.migrationPath: Do not migrate the canonical project onto it; preserve useful architectural lessons only.
records.experiment: None unless a specific isolated behavior needs comparison.
records.acceptance: No canonical dependency is introduced from the archived base.

records.fact: Shijima-Web is an experimental web version of Shijima. It is small, JavaScript-based, and not archived, but has minimal adoption and has not been pushed since January 2026.
records.fit: PCX-038 can compare browser-host behavior and pack/runtime architecture without replacing its current GameSync bridge/parser/runtime.
records.benefit: Provides an independent implementation reference for web-host edge cases.
records.risks: Experimental maturity and low adoption make it unsuitable as replacement authority.
records.migrationPath: Use only differential fixtures and behavior comparisons.
records.experiment: Run the same small Shimeji pack through current GameSync browser runtime and Shijima-Web, comparing actions, anchors, drag, fall, edge behavior, persistence, and host-page interference.
records.acceptance: Any borrowed behavior has a reproducible failing case and passes the existing GameSync browser/runtime gates; no bridge/storage/pack semantics are removed.

records.fact: The current source is a dependency-light three-file web runtime using webmeji.css, config.js, and webmeji.js. It supports bottom/side/top movement, pet interaction, pointer/touch dragging, jumping, falling, recovery, and requestAnimationFrame movement.
records.fit: PCX-039 is specifically a low-setup website-embedded companion and GameSync already contains explicit Webmeji settings/allowances.
records.benefit: Strong direct behavioral reference with minimal integration assumptions.
records.risks: Upstream README notes the core JS is messy/unoptimized and primarily developed on desktop Chrome-based browsers; it is not the user-owned canonical source.
records.migrationPath: Resolve canonical user source, diff behavior and config, then port isolated fixes/features rather than wholesale replacement.
records.experiment: Prototype arbitrary element-edge attachment and momentum as optional modules while preserving the existing three-file embed path.
records.acceptance: Existing bottom/top/left/right, pet, drag, jump, fall and multi-instance behavior remains; touch and desktop input work; host page click/scroll/navigation remains unaffected; optional features disable cleanly.

records.fact: scheduler.yield() yields main-thread work and resumes as a prioritized task, but MDN marks it Limited availability and not Baseline because some major browsers do not support it.
records.fit: Pinterest Nocturne v1.9 is explicitly built around input priority and bounded deferred page-engine work.
records.benefit: On supporting Chromium builds, it may reduce bespoke scheduling overhead and improve cooperative yielding during non-input slices.
records.risks: Firefox coverage is incomplete, browser scheduling semantics can change benchmarks, and incorrect use could delay required feed/media work.
records.migrationPath: Feature-detect scheduler.yield and retain the exact existing fallback path. Never make the API required for correctness.
records.experiment: On a proposal branch, replace only one bounded background slice boundary with feature-detected scheduler.yield and compare the existing exact 1.9 interaction/feed benchmarks.
records.acceptance: Median/p95 interaction does not regress, organic card/media counts and full fidelity remain identical, Firefox follows the existing fallback, Lean Off/Performance Off remain reversible, and live Pinterest smoke has no new console/network/runtime errors.

records.fact: web-vitals 6.0.0 is current and was published in August 2026.
records.fit: It could provide standard page performance metrics, but Pinterest Nocturne is intentionally dependency-light and already owns targeted interaction/feed fixtures.
records.risks: Adds a runtime/package dependency and generic metrics that do not directly prove Pinterest Nocturne correctness or its specialized interaction objectives.
records.migrationPath: Do not add to runtime. If useful, evaluate as an external benchmark-only dev tool.
records.experiment: Optional benchmark harness only, never production extension dependency.
records.acceptance: No production dependency added unless a specific metric materially improves release gating beyond existing tests.
